title: ONLINE-TICS: Internet-Delivered Behavioral Treatment for Patients with Chronic Tic Disorders

design.type: Prospective randomized controlled observer-blind three-arm trial at five German centers; only Hannover offered face-to-face CBIT
design.randomization: Protocol: permuted blocks, stratified by site and preexisting anti-tic medication; 1:1 online arms at four centers, initially 1:1:1 at Hannover. Planned f2f n=16, actual n=24.
design.inclusion: Adult DSM-5 TS or chronic tic disorder, sufficient German and internet access, tic severity threshold and CGI-S criterion; medication stable at least six weeks. Threshold wording differs between protocol/registry and paper; see discrepancies.
design.exclusions: Prior tic behavioral therapy; comorbidity needing primary/initial treatment; schizophrenia or pervasive developmental disorder; secondary tics or significant neurologic/psychiatric illness; current substance abuse/dependence; absent internet ability/access; recent other interventional study.
design.interventions: Completely therapist-independent internet CBIT versus a similarly delivered education control; face-to-face manualized CBIT at Hannover only. Eight regular sessions. Protocol says over ten weeks; main paper section 2.1 says eight-week treatment.
design.ongoing_exposure: iCBIT participants could use the platform during the six-month follow-up. Face-to-face participants could receive two optional boosters. Control/f2f participants could access iCBIT after their last follow-up.
design.masking: Outcome observers intended masked; participant allocation likely inferable; no genuine participant blinding. Randomization does not remove self-report expectation bias or missingness bias.
design.applicability: Direct adult evidence, but not a specifically persistent-severe adult cohort, an untreated natural-history study, or a refractory-to-CBIT sample. No diagnosis-stratified result or proof of continuously severe symptoms. Exclusions limit application to acute/unstable comorbidity and digitally excluded people.

endpoints_and_methods.primary: Baseline-to-V3 YGTSS-TTS difference in adjusted mean change, iCBIT minus psychoeducation, at one week after treatment; standalone two-sided alpha .05 / upper 95% CI below zero.
endpoints_and_methods.key_secondary: V3 YGTSS-TTS iCBIT versus face-to-face non-inferiority margin three points; confirmatory testing allowed only after primary superiority. Primary gate failed, so result is exploratory.
endpoints_and_methods.other_secondary: V4/V5 TTS, motor/vocal components, impairment, GTS-QOL and GTS-QOL-VAS, video and self-rated tics, urges, clinician global scales, comorbidity and therapeutic alliance. No verified family-wide adjustment for these exploratory outcomes in inspected sources.

visits.V3: one week after end of treatment
visits.V4: three months after end of treatment
visits.V5: six months after end of treatment

endpoints_and_methods.model: MMRM of change with baseline outcome, treatment, visit, center, anti-tic medication and treatment-by-visit; participant random effect and compound-symmetric within-person covariance; REML, between-within denominator degrees of freedom. Figure 1 specifies separate expanded models through V3, V4 and V5.
endpoints_and_methods.analysis_population: Nominal ITT includes all randomized participants; this does not mean every outcome was observed for all of them. MMRM uses an assumed missing-at-random mechanism; LOCF in secondary/sensitivity analyses; PP restricted to compliance. Numeric sensitivity estimates are not supplied in the inspected main text.
endpoints_and_methods.responder_definition: Protocol 30% TTS reduction changed to at least 25% at a reported blinded review meeting following Jeon 2013. This is a documented analysis change, not the original protocol threshold. It remains a tic-response threshold, not a GTS-QOL MCID.
endpoints_and_methods.scale_direction: For the focal TTS, impairment and GTS-QOL totals, lower is favorable. A separate prior primary study (Gerasch 2016 Methods) explicitly defines GTS-QOL-VAS higher as greater life satisfaction. Trial-specific VAS recoding was not documented in the inspected ONLINE-TICS sources.
endpoints_and_methods.qol_version_limits: German-language sample and GTS-QOL reference to original Cavanna 2008. Precise translation/scoring/domain algorithm and native-domain change contrasts were not verified; do not pool it automatically with French adaptation or invent an MCID.

urge_PUTS9_iCBIT_minus_control.interpretation: Nominally unfavorable to iCBIT under higher-worse scoring

GTS_QOL_VAS_iCBIT_minus_control.interpretation: Unfavorable under standard higher-better VAS scoring; trial coding not independently documented
Boundary value; do not round into definitive significance

ATQ_discrepancy.action: Both retained; do not choose the favorable V5 version or combine rows as independent evidence. Excluded from aggregate multiplicity computation.

other_numeric_findings.CGI_I_responder_model: Failed to converge because few met much/very much improved criterion. No joint counts or successful model estimate reconstructed.
other_numeric_findings.comorbidity: Table 4 has isolated nominal contrasts in OCD, ADHD, depression and anxiety but no consistent improvement at every visit; all four V5 contrasts include zero. No unqualified global psychiatric benefit claim.

attrition.derived_arm_counts: See aggregate_checks.json; 27/16/10 noncompliant and 40/54/14 compliant in iCBIT/control/f2f.
attrition.unidentified: Arm-by-visit outcome-specific observed n, missingness pattern, missingness-specific outcome means, and joint change covariance. Do not derive exact V3 completer or model-used sample counts from compliance.
attrition.interpretation: MAR is an assumption; LOCF and PP agreement do not demonstrate robustness to informative missingness. No MNAR tipping-point efficacy calculation supported by available aggregates.

safety.attribution: Investigators assessed none as treatment-related; open-question ascertainment.
safety.limit: Events are not participants. No observed attributed safety signal does not establish absence of rare harms or burden. Nominal group comparison is not definitive comparative safety.

funding_conflicts.funding: German Federal Ministry of Education and Research, grant 01KG1421; EUR 600 from Tourette-Gesellschaft Deutschland.
funding_conflicts.platform: Minddistrict implementation collaboration; trial investigators developed the intervention.
funding_conflicts.declarations: Main paper lists multiple research, consulting, advisory, lecture or trial-funding relationships for K. Müller-Vahl, R. Musil, V. Roessner and another investigator; others report none. Full disclosure section linked; no inference of misconduct.

source_discrepancies: Protocol abstract lists NCT02413216, a pediatric TicHelper trial; body, primary paper and official record identify ONLINE-TICS as NCT02605902.
Protocol abstract says eighty sessions; body says eight sessions over ten weeks. Main paper says eight-week treatment. Preserve visit timing relative to treatment end.
Protocol/registry use TTS >14/>10 and CGI-S >4; primary paper describes minimum scores of 14/10 and 4. Actual boundary handling not resolved.

Registry control description includes relaxation training; main paper describes psychoeducation excluding behavioral-therapy information. Do not silently equate full control content without clarification.
Table 3 impairment V5 CI upper is -1.54; Results 3.1 prose prints +1.54. Use the table for the aggregate audit, prominently retain discrepancy.
ATQ estimates, intervals and p-values in Table 4 differ from Results 3.4 prose, including V5 nominal significance.
Motor V5 p is <.001 in Table 3 and .001 in prose. Not used in the focal nine-contrast computation.

registry_snapshot.primary: YGTSS-TTS one week after end of treatment
registry_snapshot.IPD_plan: No in indexed researcher view; paper says data available on request. Neither is granted access.
registry_snapshot.limitation: Current API record and researcher-view current/original fields inspected; complete historical version chain not audited.

correction_retraction_check: No linked correction or retraction identified in inspected PubMed/primary metadata and limited exact-DOI/title search. Publisher HTML blocked by 429; this is not comprehensive clearance.
access: Institutional main-paper PDF text accessible, publisher HTML returned 429, direct PMC showed browser challenge; PDF screenshots failed. Full protocol HTML and official registry API accessible. No source full-text files or participant data saved.
supported_claim: Later exploratory randomized tic and disease-specific QoL contrasts favor iCBIT in adults under continued platform access, with separate timing and considerable missingness uncertainty.
unsupported_claims: Confirmatory or universal equivalence to face-to-face CBIT
Significant increase in efficacy over time
Tic and quality-of-life effects differ or agree at individual level
Global wellbeing improvement across every instrument
A validated meaningful-change threshold for GTS-QOL
Applicability to all severe/refractory adult patients
